description: What distribution service is near a Texas address or coordinate, for loads and generators small enough to sit on a distribution feeder (typically under about 10 MW): the nearest substations that OpenStreetMap shows with a distribution bus, with high and low side voltage, the PUCT certificated utility or co-op that serves the point, and distribution lines (under 69 kV) within a radius, each marked mapped (traced in OpenStreetMap, with voltage and operator where tagged) or modeled (gridfinder statistical model, likely route only). Use for 'can I put a 9.9 MW data center or behind-the-meter solar here', 'is there a distribution line along this parcel', 'which distribution sub would feed this', 'who is the distribution utility at this point'. Feeder capacity, hosting capacity and voltage on most lines are not public in Texas; this tells you where to look and who to call, and the utility confirms. Free shows counts and distances; Pro adds voltages, operators, line locations and station detail.

address.description: Texas street address, e.g. '1201 Main St, Houston, TX'. Use this or lat/lng.

lat.description: Latitude (WGS84). Use with lng instead of address.

lng.description: Longitude (WGS84). Use with lat instead of address.

radius_mi.description: Radius for distribution lines in miles. Default 1, max 5.

name: distribution_near
title: Distribution service near a site (small loads)
